_doc: Calibration examples injected into the chat system prompt. Each example pairs a user prompt with the ideal first-call decision: a tool to invoke, the args, and a confidence score [0.0-1.0]. Confidence < 0.6 means DO NOT call the tool — call ASK_USER instead. The `note` is for the model's benefit so it understands WHY the example chose this shape; it is included in the rendered prompt. Edit freely; the chat service reloads on import. Keep the list below ~30 entries — it ships in every chat turn's system prompt. Confidence labels are advisory, not a hard gate; the model still inspects each user message on its own.

examples.prompt: buy 10 RELIANCE at market
examples.note: Single deterministic action, all required fields present. NEVER use propose_workflow for one-shot orders.

examples.prompt: create a SIP of 5000 in NIFTYBEES on the 5th of every month
examples.note: SIP is an automation, not an agent. ALWAYS use create_sip for recurring fixed-amount investments.

examples.prompt: place a stop loss 5% below my INFY entry price
examples.note: Single action against an existing holding — create_sl_order, not propose_workflow. Anchor is avg_buy_price (already known to the system).

examples.prompt: exit all my intraday positions right now
examples.note: Immediate one-shot action. NOT an agent. Trust the verb 'right now' as 'execute immediately'.

examples.prompt: every Monday at 9:15 buy 10 NIFTYBEES at market
examples.note: Recurring schedule + single instrument + fixed qty + NO second action → propose_scheduled_order. NOT propose_workflow.

examples.prompt: every Monday 09:15 buy 5 NIFTYBEES and at Monday close sell my entire NIFTYBEES holding if RSI(14) is below 30

args._steps_summary: trigger.market_relative_time(open Mon) → action.place_order(buy 5 NIFTYBEES) → trigger.market_relative_time(close Mon) → fetch.indicator(rsi 14) → condition.numeric → fetch.portfolio → action.place_order(sell)

examples.note: TWO triggers / TWO branches in one ask → propose_workflow, NEVER propose_scheduled_order. The scheduled-order macro is single-trigger only. Whenever the prompt has 'AND … sells/buys at <other time>' or any conditional second leg, route to propose_workflow.

examples.prompt: invest 100000 equally across the top 5 steel stocks every Monday at 9:20
examples.note: Sector basket — propose_basket_allocation hydrates the screener + allocate steps. Steel is a canonical sector.

examples.prompt: every Monday 09:30 split 10000 rupees equally across HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, AXISBANK and TCS
examples.note: EXPLICIT TICKER LIST → propose_workflow with action.allocate_notional, NEVER propose_basket_allocation. The basket macro is sector-only ('top N steel stocks'); when the user names individual symbols, action.allocate_notional accepts a literal symbols list directly. One trigger + one allocate step is all that's needed.

examples.prompt: every weekday at 09:20 if NIFTY 50 is up more than 0.5% from previous close, buy 5 SBIN at market

args._steps_summary: trigger.schedule(09:20 weekday) → fetch.day_open(NIFTY 50) → fetch.prior_close(NIFTY 50) → condition.numeric (open/prior - 1 > 0.005) → action.place_order(buy 5 SBIN)

examples.note: Index-relative gate but action on a SINGLE symbol → propose_workflow, NEVER propose_basket_allocation. The basket macro forces a sector ticker list; single-symbol action with a gap condition needs the explicit fetch chain. A schedule + fetch.day_open + fetch.prior_close + condition.numeric + action.place_order is the right shape.

examples.prompt: buy 50 TCS at market when its price drops below 3500
examples.note: Single-symbol price threshold, no expiry → propose_threshold_order. ABSOLUTE price level required (not 'X% below open').

examples.prompt: buy 10 RELIANCE when RSI(14) crosses above 30
examples.note: Indicator threshold on a single symbol, no TTL → propose_threshold_order. Daily candle only.

examples.prompt: buy 10 RELIANCE if its 14-day RSI drops below 30, valid till the end of this month

args._steps_summary: trigger.indicator(RELIANCE rsi 14 < 30) → action.place_order(buy 10 RELIANCE market). Workflow carries valid_until='YYYY-MM-DD' (resolve relative date to absolute).

examples.note: TTL / EXPIRY phrases — 'valid till', 'until <date>', 'good for the month', 'till EOD', 'next 7 days', 'till Friday' — MUST go to propose_workflow, NEVER propose_threshold_order. The threshold macro has no expiry slot and would create a workflow that runs forever, the wrong intent. Resolve the relative date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD before emitting the draft.

examples.prompt: sell my entire INFY holding when it crosses 1700
examples.note: Acts on existing holding → propose_holding_action. Quantity comes from holding lookup at fire time, not the prompt.

examples.prompt: buy 5 LT at market then place a 2% stop loss and a 5% target as an OCO bracket
examples.note: OCO (one-cancels-other) bracket on a freshly-bought position is a single deterministic chat tool, NOT a workflow. NEVER call propose_holding_action or propose_workflow with symbol='OCO' — OCO is the bracket type, never the ticker. If the chat tool can't take the buy + bracket together, split into place_market_order then create_oco_order on the resulting position.

examples.prompt: sell my SBIN if NIFTY 50 drops more than 1% from today's open

args._steps_summary: trigger.schedule(*/5 mkt-hours) → fetch.quote(NIFTY 50) → fetch.relative_threshold(NIFTY 50, day_open, -1) → condition.numeric → fetch.portfolio → action.place_order(sell {{holdings.SBIN.qty}} SBIN)

examples.note: Cross-symbol rule (trigger watches one symbol, action targets another) → propose_workflow. The macro tools all bind trigger and action to the same symbol; this shape needs the polling/fetch/condition chain. Use trigger.schedule to poll, fetch.relative_threshold on the index, then act on the holding via fetch.portfolio.

examples.prompt: (meta)
examples.note: Multi-step workflow examples (P&L guard, relative threshold, gap-up buy, multi-trigger rotation, conditional buy+SL, two-branch buy/sell pair) live in the propose_workflow tool description itself, not here. The chat hop sees those when it considers calling propose_workflow. Routing examples (which tool to pick) and ASK examples (when to clarify) belong here; full JSON workflow shapes belong with the tool that consumes them.

examples.prompt: build me an agent that buys top AI stocks worth 1 lakh every Monday

args.question: ‘AI’ isn’t a canonical sector on NSE. I can map it to the IT sector (closest proxy — TCS, INFY, HCLTECH etc.) or you can give me explicit tickers. Which would you like?

examples.note: Theme not in canonical sector list. NEVER silently substitute a sector. Approximations the system supports: AI/ML/semiconductors → IT, EV → auto, green/clean/renewables → energy, fintech → private_bank+IT.

examples.prompt: buy some Tata at market

args.question: Several Tata stocks are listed — TATAMOTORS, TATASTEEL, TATAPOWER, TCS, TATACONSUM. Which one, and how many shares?

examples.note: Ambiguous symbol AND missing quantity. Two missing fields → one focused question covering both.

examples.prompt: buy 50000 of HDFCBANK

args.question: Did you mean 50,000 shares of HDFCBANK or ₹50,000 worth (≈30 shares at current price)?

examples.note: Unit ambiguity (rupees vs shares) — never assume. The numeric magnitude alone doesn't disambiguate; ask.

examples.prompt: build an agent that buys steel on dip

args.question: How big is the 'dip' — a fixed price level, a percentage from previous close, or an RSI threshold? And how much per fire (₹ amount or share count)?

examples.note: Incomplete spec — multiple critical fields missing (threshold definition, size, schedule). One focused multi-part question is fine.

examples.prompt: cancel that one
examples.note: When an active draft is in cache, the chat service handles cancel deterministically in 12ms. The model should not call any tool — the runtime intercepts.

examples.prompt: and infy

args._context_hint: Prior turn was a PE/snapshot lookup for TCS. The user wants the same lookup repeated for INFY.

examples.note: Pronoun extension — reuse the prior tool with the new symbol. If the prior was get_live_price(TCS), call get_live_price(INFY). Do NOT re-ask clarifying questions you already resolved.

examples.prompt: where should I park 200000 idle cash for a month, FD 7.2 vs liquid 6.5
examples.note: Yield/parking question — compare_yields. NOT a workflow. Tax-bracket assumption defaults to 30% if not given.

examples.prompt: what's the price of reliance
examples.note: Single-symbol price lookup. Snapshot card. NEVER use propose_workflow for a quote.

examples.prompt: show me my holdings
examples.note: Read-only portfolio query. No agent.

examples.prompt: show me the top 10 banking stocks by market cap
examples.note: Read-only sector ranking — runs through the deterministic screener path; no agent needed. If the user follows up with 'now build me an agent for those', THEN propose_basket_allocation.

examples.prompt: screen for stocks with PE under 15 and ROE above 18

args.question: Pivot v1's screener uses sector + market cap, not PE/ROE filters. I can show you the top stocks in a sector you name, or you can list specific tickers — would either work?

examples.note: Fundamentals screen NOT supported (no fundamentals data provider in v1). Be honest about the gap; don't fabricate. Suggest the workable alternatives.

examples.prompt: buy reliance the moment its 5-minute RSI crosses 70

args.question: Pivot v1 watches indicators on the daily candle, not intraday. I can wire the same RSI(14) crossing on the daily — or check every minute during market hours and act if the live price moves a fixed amount. Which would you prefer?

examples.note: Intraday tick-level indicators NOT supported (poll-based architecture, daily candles only). Surface the gap and offer the closest supported shape.

examples.prompt: backtest buy when RSI < 30 on RELIANCE over the last 5 years
examples.note: Single-indicator backtest — runs through the deterministic indicator backtest path before this prompt is even sent. If you see this kind of message hit the LLM hop, the parser failed to match shape — call run_backtest with sensible defaults rather than asking.
